newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua's Liberals ask business to hire jobless.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua's Liberals ask business to hire jobless.

text.p: Nicaraguan vice-president-elect Enrique Bolanos appealed to business leaders on Tuesday to hire one unemployed person to help his government to fulfil its promise to create 100,000 jobs.

During last month's presidential elections, won by Arnoldo Aleman of the right-wing Liberal Alliance, the Liberals promised to make employment a priority in a country where 53 percent of the labour force is short of work.
Bolanos asked "each producer, each industrialist, each factory, each business, starting in January, to, within their capacity, give a job to one fellow Nicaraguan who is unemployed."
After meeting with officials of the petroleum giant Shell Inc., Bolanos said if local businesses made this "patriotic commitment" his government would act as "a facilitator" for job creation.
Government statistics put combined unemployment and underemployment at 53 percent of the work force.

Aleman will become president of Nicaragua on January 10, barring a successful appeal by the left-wing Sandinista Front, which finished second to the Liberals. Authorities are expected to rule on the appeal between Nov. 20-22.
